text:
ashley: Heads up — saw a p99 jump (~2.5x) starting right after we ramped runtime v2.14.0 from canary to 50% at 10:20 UTC. Affects small-model traffic (<=512 tokens) with longer context churn. Any quick triage pointers?

samir: linking grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/in/g/latency/p95-p99?from=10:00&to=11:00 — p99 climbs at 10:21. p95 mostly flat.

ashley: yep looks like queueing tail. sample trace shows queue_time spiking before token generation: `queue_ms: 1200 -> 250`.

lia: surprising — v2.14.0 included the shared KV-cache shuffle (shared_kvcache=true) and a new kernel-selector heuristic. hypothesis: shared KV cache hot contention for small-model hot keys.

vikram: confirm: kernel-selector change also biases batch packing to prefer larger sequences, could increase scheduling jitter for small sequences. two simultaneous changes — bisect target.

ashley: steps I ran so far: 1) replayed small-model cohort against canary in staging — reproduced 2x p99. 2) adb logs show many `kvcache_hit` flips to `miss` under contention.

ashley: sample log snippet: ```
[10:21:23] request_id=ckj1 queue_ms=235 model=redwood-small kvcache_hit=false batch_size=4 kernel=default
[10:21:23] request_id=ckj2 queue_ms=1205 model=redwood-small kvcache_hit=false batch_size=2 kernel=selector-v2
```

samir: good repro. Next do a two-way bisect: disable shared_kvcache on one canary group and keep kernel-selector change on the other to see which axis explains p99. I can push a cohort split in 10m.

lia: +1. Also collect heap and lock contention stacks for the kvcache path during replay (`pstack` on the worker thread). Might show spin locks.

vikram: mitigation options while we bisect: 1) route affected tenants back to runtime v2.13 (rollback 25% traffic) 2) temporarily set `shared_kvcache=false` globally for small-model route via config flag 3) increase small-model instance pool to absorb jitter. Which do we want first?

ashley: customer-impacted tenants are 4 paying accounts. recommend rollback to v2.13 for 25% of traffic for those tenants + flip `shared_kvcache=false` for the cohort. Fastest to reduce p99.

support-bot: creating incident INC-2026: severity=high, impacted=4 tenants, runbook=latency-tail. Assigned: @samir, @lia, @ashley.

samir: rolling cohort split now: `POST /admin/router/split {"route":"small-models","variants":[{"runtime":"2.13","pct":25},{"runtime":"2.14","pct":75}]}` — will monitor.

ashley: after split p99 for that cohort dropped ~40% within 4m. still above baseline but better. pushing `shared_kvcache=false` on 2.14 group now via feature-flag: `ff toggle kvcache shared_kvcache --off --env=prod --route=small-models`.

lia: collecting contention stacks; attaching earliest sample: `mutex kvcache_lock contended 80% time` — seems the root cause.

vikram: ok root cause looks like shared kvcache lock contention + scheduling bias. Plan: (A) revert kernel-selector heuristic in next patch, (B) change shared_kvcache to per-tenant sharding or use fine-grained locks, (C) keep rollback split until patch verified.

ashley: thanks. I'll update incident and notify the four tenants that we mitigated with partial rollback and config flip.

sre-bot: deploybot: rollback job scheduled by @samir to runtime v2.13 for tenant cohort 'acct-*' at 10:35 UTC. ETA 3m.

support-bot: customer comms draft: "We've identified a latency regression after a runtime rollout and have applied a temporary rollback+config mitigation. Engineering is bisecting changes and will provide ETA for permanent fix." Approve?

samir: approve. logging follow-up tasks: GH-9874 (revert kernel selector heuristic), GH-9875 (kvcache fine-grained locks + perf test), GH-9876 (add targeted p99 canary tests for small-model cohorts).

ashley: adding reproduction notes to the ticket: how to replay real traffic with cohort sample (use `replay-tool --cohort small-models --rate 0.5x --duration 15m`) and capture `kvcache` metrics.

lia: final note — add a monitoring alert to detect `kvcache_lock_wait_ms > 50` sustained for 5m so we catch this earlier next time.

ashley: closing loop here. postmortem + timeline will go to #postmortems once we stabilise. :thumbsup:
